title: Minimum Domino Rotations For Equal Row
spaceBreakdown:
- no containers allocated; only a fixed set of int counters
- no recursion
- not counted: input vectors tops/bottoms
approach: A target value v can fill a row only if it appears on at least one side of every domino. Crucially, any feasible v must appear in domino 0, so we only test v ∈ {tops[0], bottoms[0]} (at most two candidates). For each candidate, scan once: if a domino has v on neither side, v is infeasible; otherwise rotations to make all tops = v is the count of indices where tops[i] ≠ v, and rotations to make all bottoms = v is the count where bottoms[i] ≠ v. Take the minimum feasible value. This is O(n) time, O(1) space.
hints: If some value v is going to fill an entire row, where must v appear in the very first domino? Also recall every face value is between 1 and 6.

Greedy counting over at most two candidate values. For v = tops[0] in Example 1 (tops = [2,1,2,4,2,2]), scan each domino: count indices where tops[i] ≠ 2 (these need a rotation to make tops all 2) → 2 rotations, feasible.

**Already uniform** - every domino already shows the same value on both rows.
`tops = [1,1], bottoms = [1,1]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: counting rotations as "number of i where bottoms[i] == v" (instead of "tops[i] != v") → returns 2.

**Only bottoms[0] is a feasible candidate** - tops[0]'s value fails at some later domino, but bottoms[0]'s value works.
`tops = [3,1,1], bottoms = [1,2,2]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: only testing candidate tops[0] and skipping bottoms[0] → returns -1.

**No feasible value** - neither candidate appears in every domino.
`tops = [3,5,1,2,3], bottoms = [3,6,3,3,4]` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: initializing ans = 0 and returning ans when no candidate is feasible → returns 0.

**tops[0] == bottoms[0]** - only one distinct candidate exists; the second iteration is redundant but harmless.
`tops = [2,2,2], bottoms = [2,3,2]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: deduplicating candidates with a set but then indexing `candidates[1]` unconditionally → undefined/out-of-range access.

followUps.q: What if face values could be up to 10^9 instead of 1..6?
followUps.a: Nothing changes - feasibility still requires v to be in domino 0, so we still test at most two candidates {tops[0], bottoms[0]}. Time stays O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if you must make BOTH rows uniform (tops all equal to a, bottoms all equal to b, a possibly ≠ b), minimizing rotations?
followUps.a: For each candidate pair (a, b) drawn from {tops[0], bottoms[0]} × {tops[0], bottoms[0]}, scan once: domino i is satisfiable with 0 rotations if (tops[i]==a and bottoms[i]==b), or 1 rotation if (bottoms[i]==a and tops[i]==b), else infeasible. With V=6 this is O(n); with arbitrary values it is O(n) per pair, still constant pairs.

followUps.q: What if dominoes arrive in a stream and you must answer after each prefix?
followUps.a: Track, for each of the 6 values, a feasibility flag and two rotation counts (top-misses and bottom-misses). On each new domino, update the 6 counters and invalidate any value absent from both faces. Answer after each step is the min feasible count. O(1) per domino, O(6) = O(1) space.
